links.outcome: Reading level of existing neurosurgical patient education materials versus eighth-grade level
links.effect: Mean FRE for PEMs on all 5 neurosurgical conditions were significantly greater than eighth-grade reading level scores (P < .001); Kincaid, ARI, Coleman-Liau, Gunning Fog, SMOG all significantly above eighth grade (P < .01).
links.quote: The mean Kincaid value, Automated Readability Index, Coleman-Liau score, Gunning Fog Index, and Simple Measure of Gobbledygook Index for PEMs on each condition were all significantly greater than an eighth-grade reading level ( P < .01).

links.outcome: Readability of hospital-published patient education materials relative to average American reading level
links.effect: Existing PEMs from top US hospitals exceeded eighth-grade reading level on all readability measures (FRE P < .001; other indices P < .01).
links.quote: Existing PEMs published by the top US hospitals for common neurosurgical conditions may be too complicated for the average American that reads at an eighth-grade level.

links.outcome: Readability and accuracy of rewritten PEMs
links.effect: 25 PEMs were rewritten; authors concluded lower reading level with maintained accuracy, with rewritten FRE lower (P<.01) except spinal stenosis (P=.104).
links.quote: Large language model chatbots can be used to efficiently rewrite these PEMs at a lower reading level while maintaining the accuracy of the material.

links.outcome: readability and accuracy of rewritten patient education materials
links.effect: Mean FRE score for rewritten PEMs was significantly lower than nonrewritten materials (P < .01) except spinal stenosis (P = .104); accuracy was validated.
links.quote: The mean FRE score for rewritten PEMs on each topic were significantly lower than nonrewritten materials ( P < .01) except spinal stenosis ( P = .104) and were validated for accuracy.
